ILO direct-path 403 flap: fourth occurrence at cycle 166 (2026-08-08T00:01:22Z) - 5 of 12 contract assertions broken (references:all, children, descendants, parents, parentsandsiblings), resolved by the time of this run's live recheck (~40 min later). Prior occurrences: cycle 32, cycle 94, cycle 159 (broadest yet at 10 of 12). All four resolved within one cycle. Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy throughout every occurrence - only contract-probe traffic drew the 403. IMPORTANT: /api/history's per-endpoint status/failing series does NOT reflect contract-probe-only degradation. Future runs must check /api/cycle/{id} for every intermediate cycle since the last run, not rely on /api/history or /api/contracts changes (which only diffs the two newest cycles) alone. Watch for a fifth ILO occurrence, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle.

IMF references:* 401 flap: first occurrence, cycle 161 (14:01:22Z) - 4 of the references:* contract assertions (all, children, descendants, parentsandsiblings) returned HTTP 401 where 200 was expected, resolved by cycle 162, clean through cycle 166 (no recurrence). Same shape as the recurring ILO 403 flap (probe volume tripping provider-side throttling, not a general IMF outage). Watch for a second occurrence; a second episode soon would elevate this from one-off to a recognized pattern like ILO's.
